# R4-pixel frozen tables (generated by gen/r4gen.py; the .txt tables and .tsv predictions are the frozen files)

Sets: control, heldout, repeat, replicate.  Stage order: p4-o4, q4-v, q4-f, q4-t, g4-rw.  Quantity = value [hypothesis].

## p4-o4

Q276 o4 clause (pixel), stage p4-o4: which o4 word lands.  E808: with 5' (tag 13, bit 3) and 5 written in both orders every o4 word read
tag 5.  Model family: single-write path V1 (drops bit 3), V2 (a word with bit 3 does not land), V3 (as written) x combine last, first, and,
or, min, the 12 that fit E808 (score/o4model.py).  Words differ in other bits too: A4 = tag 5 + bit 4, A5 = tag 5 + bit 5; the job marker
sits at bits 15:6.  Rows: 8 controls (c-e709, c-o4-u, c-o4s-u, c-u: G-o4, tag 5, tag 5, G-o1), 14 value jobs (7 configurations x x/y: A3,
A4, A then A4, A4 then A, A then A5, A5 then A, A3 then A4), 12 predicate jobs (p1 A / !p1 A4 and the swapped order, k = 0, 3, 7: gated =
only the instance whose lane equals k writes through p1, ignored = both writes run), 2 replicates of c-o4-u.  The predicate rows are read
only if the bit-4 pairs read two classes in the two orders.  No fault is expected; any fault or hang stops the stage.

## q4-v

Stage q4-v (Q082, TA side): bit 7 held out against the TA-clock rule (28 jobs; plan section 3.1, decisions R4-9 a and the user's
bit-7 scope a: q4-v as written, the 1500-vertex rows included).

The rule (round 4's offline reading, E807's corrections, hw_spec EVENT_STATUS2: SEMI on E807's 74 jobs): with L the longest run of
regtimeline samples with CR_CLKGATESTATUS (0x0008) == 0x000ccff8 (the TA's clocks while it works on the vertices), bit 7 of STATUS2 is
set after the job iff L >= 129.5 us (clear below 122 us, set above 136 us, the edge between is not scored), and it shows 118 to 138 us
after that run began.  [infer] the latch means: the TA made no progress for about 125 to 130 us.  Rows: controls v-ctl0, v-n1, v-i880,
v-i1760 (the bridge to E807 on the rgn4 module: 0x400 / clear / clear with L 95 to 112 / set); three ladders of bodies and vertex
counts E807 never ran, b12v (10 multiply-adds, 13 instructions an iteration, 3 vertices), b2v (counter and branch only, 2
instructions, 3 vertices) and b8v on 24 vertices, each two FIT points (clear by the model, run first) and five HELD OUT points at
0.80, 0.92, 1.08, 1.20 and 1.60 x N* (N* from the frozen offline model of L, score/r4const.py); and the stock program with 1500
vertices at 2048x2048 (twice) and 4096x4096: H-STALL (no progress is what latches: clear, as the ten 1500-vertex jobs of R3-geo's
g-c4) against H-PHASE (the TA phase's length latches: set); a job whose L is below 125 us is void for that.  Every job runs under
regtimeline 0x0008, 0x0118, 0x012c and reads STATUS2 after the reset (0x400 else the stage stops) and after the job.  The loop
proof of a vertex loop is the stored depth word 0x3f200000 + N at every decoded vertex.  A bridge control that reads otherwise
stops the session (runner knob want2).

## q4-f

Stage q4-f (Q082, pixel side, the load; 16 jobs, plan section 3.2): what a load does to the latch of bit 6 in a fill.

Round 3 (E805): every ALU body set bit 6 in a fill when its tile time (B - 60.2) / 4 passed about 125 us and the body with a load and
a wait (ld8: a load, a wait, 4 multiply-adds, counter, branch) never did, to 320 iterations and 13.4 ms bursts.  Three readings:
H-YIELD (a wait ends a piece of work: the timer restarts at every load), H-LOADOFF (a program that waits on a load never latches) and
H-SUM (the busy time of the tile, waits not counted, is summed: a long sum sets it, which ld8's data already make unlikely).  Rows:
the bridge to E804 / E805 on the rgn4 module (the relative b8 loop at 16, 53, 56, 136 iterations and ld8 at 70: c, c, S, S; c);
ld0-K: ONE load and wait, then the b8 loop K times (K = 28, 53, 70, 110); ldo-K-M: M times (load, wait, the b8 loop K times) for
(K, M) = (28, 4) (28, 16) (40, 8) (70, 1) (70, 4) (110, 2) (220, 1).  The frozen table (plan 3.2):
  H-YIELD    ld0 28, 53, 70, 110: c, either, S, S   ldo (28,4) (28,16) (40,8): c, c, c   ldo (70,1) (70,4) (110,2) (220,1): S, S, S, S
  H-LOADOFF  ld0: c, c, c, c                        ldo (first three): c, c, c           ldo (last four): c, c, c, c
  H-SUM      ld0: c, either, S, S                   ldo (first three): S, S, S           ldo (last four): S, S, S, S
sgx-pipe's `events::status2_bit6` (the rule over a tile's time, a 64 x 32 fill WITHOUT a load, clear below 118 us, set above 132 us,
refused between) agrees with the bridge rows where it speaks: at 16 iterations (tile time 36 us) clear, at 136 (307 us) set, and it
REFUSES 53 and 56 (119.5 and 126.5 us, inside its edge): those two predictions are E804's measured bracket (2 of 2 each), not the rule's.
Every load row is outside the rule (a fill with a load is refused by status2_bit6, E805's ld8): the three readings are what is tested.
The time of the latch d6 is recorded with no prediction (round 4's timing model of the latch was refuted on the older data).  Two-level
counters; MARK only when both counters end (o0 = MARK on 2048 of 2048), every program checked in sgx-sim at code index 0.  A bridge
control that reads otherwise stops the session (runner knob want2).

## q4-t

Stage q4-t (Q082, pixel side, triangles; 54 jobs, plan section 3.3; decision: triangles a, the t6 row, without 2x2).

`probe --tri pixel --temps 32 --width W --height H --tri-full "loop"` with the relative b8 loop and MARK, as E806 (round 3's q-t).  E806
first set bit 6 at 56 iterations (32x16, 32x32, 128x128: clear at 53) and at 110 (8x8, 16x16, 64x32, 256x256) and at 220 (4x4); the
tile time of every size at its last clear and first set point brackets 120 to 160 us (slope a tile 0.72 us / N at 4x4, 1.65 at 8x8,
2.5 at 16x16 and 64x32; qt_slopes.out).  H-SEG: bit 6 latches when the pixel side makes no progress for about 125 us, progress being
the end of a piece of work that is at most a tile; H-N: the threshold is a pass count near 57 to 62 at every size; E806-DISC: the first
set point of a size is 56 or 110 (220 at 4x4) as E806 read it, discrete.  Rows (frozen, plan 3.3):
  controls (12, set control): the stock green triangle and the loop at N = 1 at 4x4, 8x8, 16x16, 32x16, 64x32 (MARK on W x H of W x H
    / green), and the fill (probe without --tri) at 53 and 56: clear, set (the bridge to E804 on the rgn4 module; want2 stops the
    session if it reads otherwise);
  8x8 at 60, 66, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104 (H-SEG: 60 and 66 clear, 104 set, first set 72 to 104; H-N: 66 and up set; E806-DISC: all clear);
  4x4 at 80, 110, 140, 170, 200 (H-SEG: 80, 110, 140 clear; H-N: set from 80; E806-DISC: all clear to 200);
  16x16, 32x16 and 64x32 at 46, 56, 56 again, 60, 66, 72 (H-SEG: 46 clear, 66 and 72 set at all three, 56 and 60 either; H-N the same;
    E806-DISC: 32x16 set from 56, the other two clear to 72);
  64x32 and 8x8 at 150, 180, 250, 330 (set; the first-piece reading: t6 = 250 + 0.43 N us after the burst starts to N = 290, 250 beyond,
    +- 15 us; the t6 rows are the only test of that reading: if they fail the bit rule can still hold);
  the default (partial) 64x64 triangle at 150, 200, 280, 400 (exploratory: no prediction).
H-SEG is refuted by 16x16 or 64x32 clear at 72, by 8x8 set at 60 or clear at 104, by 4x4 set at 110; E806-DISC by a size that sets at 66
where it predicts clear (8x8, 16x16, 64x32) or clear at 66 at 32x16.  sgx-pipe's status2_bit6 (a 64 x 32 fill without a load) stays
refused for a triangle and agrees with the fill controls (clear at 53 is the edge row of the bridge: it refuses 53 and 56 as in q4-f).

## g4-rw

Q230 (geometry), g4-rw: a table of 60 w, three a job (w3 = 0.75 w1 + 0.25 w2 on the tool's triangle: two free, one derived),
in R2's t3-nocut shape (vtx_zw.s: z = 0, w = C x + D, no clip, window 32 + 32 x / w, vertices in input order).  C and D are chosen so
that every w is computed exactly in float32 (fused or not).  40 designed w: the 31 grid mantissas 1 + k/32 and 9 others with fine
low bits; a third of the jobs at scale 1, a third at 4, a third at 1/4.  Controls (4, first): w = 1; (3, 9, 4.5); (7, 10, 7.75);
(1.40625, 1.78125, 1.5): the known words exact.  Frozen: every word is RZ or RZ + 1 of 1/w; the 60 w split 30 FIT / 30 HELD OUT by the
sha256 of their bits.  After the run: the families of score/rwfam.py fitted on FIT, scored on HELD OUT; more than one family at 30 of
30 held out, or none: the words are recorded and no rule is adopted.
